answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote or claim rewards, then slash that stake when a randomly selected audit proves coordinated fraud. The audit can compare signed work histories and payment flows, not merely profile names, so splitting one operator across many accounts does not multiply trustworthy influence. A pigment tag may be a signal for review, like a willow account’s sudden burst of linked claims; it is evidence to investigate, not proof by itself. Sybils remain possible, but each one ties up capital and risks forfeiture.
